The 2x edit is no stronger than 1x (190 vs 192 on hard328) and at about RL strength on MATH-500, so it keeps about RL's MATH-500 cap hits (~7-8, T2). f2-m03 multiplies the stop hazard with dose: hard328 cap hits 77 -> 5 at 2x (x0.065), so the cued base's ~22.5 per sample on MATH-500 falls to ~2.

cells.readout: right answers with grader v3 (metrics.json; cap hits wrong)
cells.why: r6-m06 puts the base's wrong steps in the head of its distribution, so cutting the deep tail leaves the score at the untruncated cue level (405-418, mean 410.5), minus a little for loops. f2-m04 makes the base's errors chance slips drawn independently at each step. A cut that removes low-probability draws then removes about half of the ~31 slip-type wrong answers (35 % of ~90), giving about +15 before a small loop cost.

cell.n: 51 items; readout on the 35 items labelled misread (14) or slip (21)

cells.readout: right continuations (v3, cap hits wrong unless a gradable answer is present, as in result-a497ff) among the 140 continuations of the misread- and slip-labelled items
cells.why: r7-m05 says misreads and slips are the problem-free prior's continuation, so a stronger contrast against the problem-free context lowers both: misreads rise from 32 % (no contrast) past alpha 1's 43 % to about 50 %, and slips rise from 49 % to about 55 %. f2-m03 says a misreading is set up by the problem's wording, which the contrast amplifies, so misreads stay at or below 0.32 * 56 and slips stay at their chance rate (0.49 * 84). That gives about 56.

best_base.note: no count exists on these 140 continuations. Scaled from the alpha-1 problem-contrast arm (6 continuations per item, cap 4,000): misreads 36 of 84, slips unchanged at the base's 49 % of 126. Times 4/6, that is 24 + 41 = 65 of 140.
